review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the one visible repeat against the other sources. `isSimpleRing_even_of_odd_finrank` and `isCentral_even_of_odd_finrank` both start by calling `exists_nonempty_algEquiv_even_of_odd_finrank` and then pass `by simpa using hn` to the even-dimensional theorem. That is routine unpacking, so a shared lemma would not meet the rubric. The `isCentral` proof also repeats the short transport argument of Mathlib's `Algebra.IsCentral.of_algEquiv`, because that lemma needs both algebras in one universe. The comment in the file says so. The argument is two lines. The same `MulEquivClass.apply_mem_center_iff` step appears in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Even/Center.lean` around line 217, but there it is a one-line sub-step of a much larger proof. A universe-polymorphic lemma would be a thin wrapper, so I do not count it as a finding. The remaining theorems (`exists_reversalEquiv_even_of_finrank_pos`, the two existence corollaries, the two degree theorems) share no nontrivial reasoning. I could not run Lean.
